title: Incident report: speaker names mixed up in a training transcript
summary: Báo cáo giải thích vì sao tên người nói trong bản chép lời bị gán sai, cách nhóm xác định phạm vi ảnh hưởng và quyết định kiểm tra trước khi xử lý lại.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: On Thursday morning, the learning team opened the transcript of a recorded customer-service workshop. The words were mostly correct, but several comments appeared under the wrong speaker names. A question from a new employee was shown as advice from the trainer, which changed how the conversation looked. The recording itself played normally. Because the transcript would become part of an internal training pack, the team stopped preparing the pack and contacted the software team. This report explains what happened, how we checked the affected files, and why we chose a slower correction process before allowing the material to be shared.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The workshop had been recorded in three sections, with a short break between each section. Our transcript service processed those sections separately and then joined the results. Each section contained numbered speaker labels, such as Speaker 1 and Speaker 2. The numbers described voices within one section; they did not identify the same people across the whole workshop. However, our joining step treated matching numbers as matching people. When the trainer spoke second after the break, her comments received the name previously attached to the second voice. The error came from our joining step, rather than from the original recording.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: We first considered correcting only the names reported by the learning team. That would have produced a usable document quickly, but it could have left less obvious mistakes elsewhere. Instead, we compared every speaker change in the transcript with the recording. Two colleagues worked independently and marked any disagreement for a second listen. They also checked whether the text had moved between sections. No text was missing from this workshop, although three speaker names were wrong. That distinction mattered: we needed to correct the identity attached to certain comments without suggesting that the spoken content had been lost or rewritten.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Our file list showed that eight other recordings had used the same joining step since its introduction on Monday. Five contained only one section and did not need their speaker labels joined. The other three were removed from the shared training folder while we checked them. One had the same naming problem; the remaining two used a single speaker throughout. We informed the owners of all nine recordings, including those without an identified error. The message described the confirmed problem and the checks still in progress. It did not promise that every transcript was accurate simply because its speaker names looked reasonable.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: For the immediate correction, we assigned speaker names separately within each section before joining the text. The learning team supplied a participant list, but a name on that list was not enough to identify a voice. We used the trainer's introductions and direct address in the recording as supporting evidence. Where identity remained uncertain, we kept a neutral speaker label. The training owner accepted this limitation because a clear unknown label was more useful than a confident mistake. Corrected copies included a revision note, and the original shared copies were replaced only after the owner had reviewed the revised names.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The proposed permanent change will keep section labels separate until a reviewer confirms which voices belong to the same person. This adds a review task, so the learning team asked whether it could be skipped for recordings with one speaker. We agreed to support that simpler route when the owner explicitly confirms that only one person speaks. For conversations, the review screen will show a short audio sample beside each proposed identity. We rejected automatic name matching based only on speaker numbers. That option was cheaper to build, but it repeated the assumption that had caused the incident in the first place.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Before restoring the joining service, we will test recordings in which participants speak in different orders after a break. We will also include a section where one participant remains silent and another joins late. These examples reflect the conditions our earlier checks missed. The service owner will record the result of each test and ask a learning-team reviewer to inspect the final transcript. Until those checks pass, longer workshops will use the separate-section process. The incident has delayed the training pack by two working days, but the learning team prefers that delay to distributing advice under the wrong person's name.

title: Demonstration procedure: preparing an office visit without exposing customer details
summary: Quy trình chuẩn bị buổi trình diễn tại văn phòng, phân công người phụ trách, chọn dữ liệu mẫu và xử lý câu hỏi hoặc yêu cầu thay đổi phút cuối.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Next Wednesday, twelve students from a local technical college will visit our office to see how a small software company works. The visit includes a short product demonstration, a discussion with two engineers, and a tour of the shared working area. During our last visit, a presenter opened a recent customer record while answering an unexpected question. No copy was shared, but the customer's name appeared on the large screen. This procedure gives the new visit a clear preparation process. Its purpose is to make the demonstration useful while keeping real customer details out of the material visitors can see.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Mai will own the visit schedule, while Daniel will own the demonstration content. These responsibilities are separate because a room change should not automatically change what the presenter shows. By Monday afternoon, Daniel must send Mai the demonstration outline and the names of everyone who will speak. The outline should describe the visitor's journey through the product, rather than list every available feature. The college has asked for examples of ordinary working decisions, so we will show how a team receives a request, checks its details, and agrees on a next step. A fifteen-minute demonstration leaves time for questions afterward.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The presenter must use the visitor account, which contains invented projects and customer names. This account has enough information to show the main workflow without opening the live customer area. On Tuesday, a colleague who is not presenting will follow the outline using that account. The colleague will check the visible names, browser tabs, downloaded files, and any messages that appear during the demonstration. Simply replacing names on the first screen is insufficient because later screens may display related information. The reviewer should record any unsuitable material and ask Daniel to correct it before the final practice session that afternoon.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: We considered showing screenshots instead of the working product. Screenshots would make the order easier to control, but they would hide how the presenter responds when information changes. We therefore chose a live demonstration through the visitor account, supported by a small set of prepared images. If the product becomes unavailable, the presenter can use those images to explain the same journey. The backup should support the agreed story, rather than become a longer presentation with extra features. Daniel will save the approved images in the visit folder so another speaker can find them without searching through personal files.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Questions are welcome, including questions that the outline does not cover. However, the presenter should not open a real customer record to provide a more exciting answer. If an example is unavailable in the visitor account, the presenter can explain the general process or offer to prepare an invented example later. Mai will keep a question list during the session. Each unanswered question will have a named colleague responsible for preparing a response. We will send the college one combined follow-up document, which avoids several employees giving different answers separately. No delivery date should be promised until the responsible colleague has checked availability.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The office tour also needs preparation. Team leads should remove customer names from whiteboards in the route area by Tuesday evening. Desks outside that route do not need to be rearranged, but visitors should remain with their guide. Engineers who want to discuss a current project should prepare a general description before the visit. We are not asking colleagues to pretend that work is always tidy or easy. In fact, a short explanation of a difficult decision may be more useful than a perfect success story. The guide should connect these examples to the students' interests without discussing a customer's private situation.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: On Wednesday morning, Mai and Daniel will complete a final check together. Mai will confirm the room, timing, and visitor numbers; Daniel will confirm the account, presentation, and backup images. If the college requests an extra topic at the door, Daniel will decide whether the existing material can cover it safely and clearly. A last-minute request does not require an immediate demonstration. After the students leave, the two owners will collect feedback from speakers and the college coordinator. They will record which examples helped visitors understand the work and which questions need better preparation before the next office visit is arranged.

title: Borrowing notice: reserving tools for a weekend home project
summary: Thông báo của thư viện dụng cụ hướng dẫn đặt trước, nhận và trả đồ, đồng thời giải thích cách xử lý dụng cụ chưa chắc chắn về tình trạng.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The neighbourhood tool library will introduce reservations next month after several busy Saturdays left members waiting for equipment. Until now, tools have been borrowed in order of arrival, which worked well when the collection was small. Recently, several people travelled to the library expecting to borrow the same carpet cleaner. Some had already moved furniture at home before discovering that it was unavailable. The new process should help members plan ordinary home projects more reliably. It will begin with our most frequently borrowed items, while smaller hand tools will continue to be available without a reservation during normal opening hours.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Members can request an item through the library website or ask a volunteer to enter a request at the desk. Requests open fourteen days before the collection date. Each reservation covers one item for a three-day loan, including the collection day. The system shows a request as pending until a volunteer checks that the previous borrower has returned the item and that all listed parts are present. A pending request is not a confirmed booking. Members should wait for the confirmation message before arranging work that depends on the tool. Confirmation normally arrives by noon on the day before collection.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: We considered confirming every booking immediately, but a late return could then leave the next member with a promise we could not keep. The checking stage makes planning slightly less certain at first, yet it gives a more reliable answer once confirmation arrives. Members who need equipment on a fixed date should explain that in their request. A volunteer can discuss another available item or suggest choosing a different project date. The library cannot guarantee an identical replacement for every tool. We prefer to explain the available choices clearly rather than encourage members to prepare for equipment that may not arrive.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Confirmed reservations are held until eleven o'clock on the collection morning. If you expect to arrive later, contact the desk before that time so a volunteer can agree on a revised collection time. Without a message, the item may be offered to someone waiting at the library. At collection, the volunteer and borrower will compare the contents with the parts card kept inside the case. Please allow ten minutes for this check. You will also receive the manufacturer's instructions where these are available. Volunteers can explain the borrowing process, but they do not provide training for every possible use of each tool.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Please return borrowed items to the desk during opening hours, with their cases and listed accessories. The outdoor book-return box is not suitable for tools. A volunteer will check the item with you and record anything that needs attention. Normal signs of use should be mentioned, even when the tool still works. If something stops working during your loan, stop using it and contact the library to arrange the return. Do not attempt a repair on behalf of the library. A clear description of what happened is useful because it helps our equipment volunteer decide what should be checked next.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Members have asked whether every late return will lead to a borrowing restriction. During the first month, volunteers will focus on finding out why returns are late and helping members choose realistic loan periods. Repeated late returns will be discussed with the member before another reservation is accepted. The aim is to keep equipment moving between households, not to create an argument over a single difficult afternoon. If your project takes longer than expected, request an extension before the return time. An extension is possible only when it does not affect another confirmed borrower, so please prepare a backup plan.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The library will review the reservation process after six weeks. We will count confirmed loans, cancelled requests, late collections, and occasions when an item was unavailable because it needed checking. Members can leave comments on a paper form at the desk, including suggestions from people who do not use the website. If reservations reduce wasted journeys without creating too much work for volunteers, we may add more equipment to the system. For now, please reserve only items you expect to use and cancel promptly if your plans change. That small step gives another household time to organise its own project.

title: Migration proposal: making project file names work across computers
summary: Đề xuất chuẩn hóa tên tệp trong thư viện dự án, xử lý các cặp tên dễ xung đột và chuyển đổi theo từng giai đoạn để bảo vệ liên kết đang được sử dụng.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our design-export library contains drawings, reference images, and short notes used by both office staff and external contractors. Last month, a contractor reported that two downloaded files appeared to replace each other on her computer. In the library, one was named Panel.png and the other panel.png. They showed different versions of a display panel, but their names differed only in the capital letter. Our own download test reproduced the contractor's problem with her usual setup. This proposal recommends a naming migration that gives every current file a clearly distinct name without changing the contents or removing access to older project material.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The immediate problem is limited to names that become identical when capital letters are ignored. We should not assume that every member uses the same file system or download method. To understand the scope, we examined the names in active project folders and found eighteen conflicting pairs. Some represented genuine revisions; others were unrelated images uploaded by different people. We also found names with extra spaces at the end, but those will be recorded for a later review. Expanding this migration to every naming issue would delay the confirmed fix and make it harder for project owners to understand what needs their approval.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: We propose a simple pattern consisting of a project code, a descriptive name, and a revision number. For example, the two panel files could become K42-panel-front-r1.png and K42-panel-front-r2.png, once their owner confirms that they are revisions of the same drawing. The migration script will not decide that relationship from the existing names alone. A project owner must inspect the conflicting files and choose suitable descriptions. Where two files serve different purposes, their descriptive names should explain that difference. The goal is clear identification during ordinary work, rather than a naming pattern that merely satisfies an automated technical check.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Changing names can affect instructions, messages, and documents that refer to those files. Before approving a proposed name, the owner will list the places where the old name is still used. Links created through the library already use a file identifier, so our tests showed that those links continued to open after a rename. Written directions such as 'download Panel.png' still needed editing. We therefore recommend updating the project handover notes at the same time as the files. For one month, the library page will display the previous name beside the new name to help people recognise material they used earlier.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: We considered renaming every file automatically by adding a unique number. That would avoid the confirmed conflicts quickly, but names such as image-173 would tell users little about the contents. It would also make an unnecessary change to thousands of files that currently work well. The proposed migration covers only the conflicting pairs in active projects. Archived projects will remain available through the library, with a warning on download where a known name conflict exists. Their owners can request a separate correction when the material is needed again. This approach keeps the first migration small enough to review carefully and explain clearly.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The first trial will use one project with four conflicting pairs and a contractor who regularly downloads its files. We will copy the project into a practice area, apply the approved names there, and ask the contractor to complete a normal task. The task includes downloading several images, finding the correct revision, and following an existing library link. A successful technical rename is only one part of the result. If the contractor cannot recognise the files or chooses the wrong revision, the naming pattern needs improvement before it is applied elsewhere. The owner will also review the updated directions for missing references.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: After the trial, we plan to migrate the remaining active projects over two afternoons. Uploads to each project will pause briefly while its names are changed and checked. We will keep a record connecting every old name to its new name, together with the owner's approval. If a mistake is discovered, that record will guide a correction; we will not guess from memory. Future uploads will be checked for the same kind of conflict before acceptance. The service team will explain rejected names with a suggested change, so users can resolve the issue without learning the details of different computer file systems.

title: Event handover: sharing the work at a careers information stand
summary: Bản bàn giao chuẩn bị gian thông tin nghề nghiệp, phân chia ca trực, hướng dẫn trả lời câu hỏi và ghi nhận yêu cầu liên hệ mà không hứa quá phạm vi.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our company will have an information stand at Saturday's community careers event. The stand is intended for people who want to understand our work and the kinds of skills we use. It is not an interview desk, and attendance will not give anyone priority for a future vacancy. Last year, two experienced colleagues answered nearly every question while newer volunteers mainly handed out leaflets. This year, we want a more balanced arrangement that gives visitors useful answers and volunteers a clear role. These handover notes cover preparation, the rota, questions that need follow-up, and the information we should collect after the event.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The stand will open at nine and close at four, with three overlapping volunteer shifts. Each shift includes one colleague from engineering and one from another department, so visitors can hear about different kinds of work. Volunteers should arrive fifteen minutes before their shift to receive a brief handover. The overlap is working time, rather than a spare break, because it allows the incoming pair to hear about unfinished conversations and changes to the day's arrangements. Rina will coordinate the rota and keep one reserve volunteer available during the busiest period. Tell her early if your expected arrival time changes.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before Saturday, every volunteer should read the two-page information sheet in the event folder. It includes our current team structure, the published application route, and three examples of ordinary working tasks. We chose tasks from different departments because software companies need more than programmers. Volunteers may add their own experiences, but they should make clear when they are describing personal experience rather than a company-wide practice. If two colleagues give different examples, that can help visitors understand the variety of work. However, facts about the application process must follow the information sheet so that visitors receive a consistent explanation.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Visitors may ask about salary, working hours, or the exact skills needed for a role that is not currently advertised. Do not invent an answer to keep the conversation moving. Explain which information is available and offer the published careers page where appropriate. If a question needs a later response, ask whether the visitor wants to leave an email address on a follow-up card. Record the question in their own words as far as possible. A useful card explains what the visitor wants to know; a note saying only 'interested in jobs' gives the office team too little information to respond meaningfully.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: At each handover, the outgoing pair should report any practical problem and identify follow-up cards that need clarification. Cards will be placed in the closed collection box behind the stand, rather than left beside the leaflets. Volunteers should not photograph the cards or copy addresses into personal phones. We considered using a shared tablet, but the event hall's connection was unreliable during the organiser's test. Paper cards give us a simple method that does not depend on that connection. After the event, the office coordinator will transfer the requests into our agreed tracking sheet and keep the cards in the office cabinet.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: We expect some visitors to arrive in groups from the college, while others will come alone. When a group is waiting, one volunteer can give a short general explanation while the other continues an individual conversation. Avoid turning every answer into a long speech. A visitor who asks about one task may not need a complete history of the company. There will be two chairs beside the stand for conversations that benefit from a quieter pace. Volunteers should ask visitors what they want to understand before choosing an example, rather than assume that age or clothing tells us their interests or experience.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At closing time, the final pair will count unused leaflets, pack the display, and give the collection box to Rina. On Monday, the office coordinator will group the follow-up questions and assign each group to a colleague who can answer it. We aim to send responses during that week, but a difficult question may need a message explaining when an answer will be ready. The event review will consider the quality of conversations as well as visitor numbers. Please bring one example of a useful exchange and one improvement for next time, especially if the preparation sheet did not support a question you received.

title: Coach notice: joining a weekend service with limited luggage space
summary: Thông báo về chuyến xe khách cuối tuần giải thích cách khai báo hành lý lớn, xác nhận điểm đón và lựa chọn khi sức chứa không đủ.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: From the first weekend in November, the Green Valley coach service will use a smaller vehicle on its Saturday morning journey. Passenger numbers have been lower during the colder months, but several travellers still carry large bags for family visits or outdoor trips. The smaller coach has enough seats for the usual number of passengers, although its luggage space is more limited. This notice explains how to tell us about large items before travelling and how the driver will organise collection points. The Sunday evening return will continue to use the larger vehicle until the service is reviewed in December.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: When buying a Saturday ticket, passengers should select either a small bag or a large bag in the booking form. A small bag must fit beneath the seat in front without blocking the aisle. A large bag travels in the storage area under the coach. The form asks for approximate dimensions because two light but bulky bags can occupy more space than several compact suitcases. Weight alone does not tell us whether everything will fit. If you have already bought a ticket, use the link in your confirmation message to add your bag details by Thursday evening before the journey.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Unusual items, such as a folded market trolley or a musical instrument in a hard case, need a separate enquiry. Please describe the item and give its dimensions rather than choosing the nearest ordinary bag category. The booking team will check the available space and reply before confirming that the item can travel. A passenger ticket confirms a seat, but it does not automatically confirm space for an unusual item. We considered accepting everything at the roadside, as we did on quiet journeys last winter. That approach would be unfair when the driver has to choose between items after passengers have already arrived.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: If there is not enough space for your declared luggage, the booking team will explain the available choices before the travel day. These may include another departure or a smaller luggage arrangement, depending on your plans. Do not remove essential contents merely to meet the bag category shown on the form; ask us to check a realistic alternative. We will not ask the driver to place large bags in the passenger aisle. Our aim is to resolve the space problem early, while passengers still have time to change arrangements. A clear reply to our message helps us finalise the luggage list for everyone.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The coach will collect passengers at the station forecourt and then at the north-side village shop. Your confirmation message will name one collection point. Please use that point unless the booking team agrees to a change, because the driver uses separate passenger lists for the two stops. Arrive ten minutes before the stated departure time and keep your ticket available. At the station, wait beside the blue shelter rather than near the taxi entrance. The coach cannot remain there while someone searches the building for a missing traveller. If you are delayed, contact the number printed in your confirmation message.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: At boarding, the driver will check your name and luggage category against the list. Put a name label on each large bag, and keep tickets, keys, and items needed during the journey with you. The driver will load bags according to where passengers leave the coach, so your case may not be placed beside another case belonging to your family. This arrangement reduces the number of bags that must be moved at intermediate stops. Please avoid opening the storage doors yourself. At your destination, wait for the driver to unload and check the label before taking a similar-looking bag away.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The December review will compare bookings with actual travel, including how often declared bags were larger than expected and how many passengers needed another departure. We also want comments from people who found the booking form difficult. You can explain the problem to the ticket-office staff, who will add your feedback to the review. A smaller vehicle helps keep this lightly used journey running, but the arrangement must remain practical for the people who rely on it. If the luggage checks create repeated problems, we will consider changing the vehicle plan rather than simply asking passengers to bring less every week.

title: Release plan: choosing which folders stay available offline
summary: Kế hoạch phát hành tính năng chọn thư mục ngoại tuyến, làm rõ sự khác nhau giữa bỏ bản sao trên máy và xóa tệp, cùng cách kiểm thử khi đang làm việc.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our desktop project app currently keeps an offline copy of every folder a user can access. This is convenient for people who travel between sites, but it creates problems for colleagues who need only a small part of a large project. One survey team member reported that old reference photographs occupied most of the space assigned to the app on her laptop. She still needed access to those photographs occasionally, so removing herself from the project was not a useful solution. The next release will let users choose which folders remain available offline while keeping their normal access to the shared project.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The new settings page will list project folders with a simple offline switch beside each one. Turning a switch off means that the app can remove its local copy after checking for unfinished changes. It does not delete the shared folder. When connected, the user can still open its contents through the project view. When disconnected, the folder name remains visible, but the app will explain that its contents require a connection. We chose to keep the name visible because an absent folder might lead users to think that someone had removed it from the project or changed their access without warning.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The most important protection concerns work that has not yet reached the shared project. If a user turns off offline access while a file contains local changes, the app will keep that file and show a waiting message. The local copy will be removed only after those changes have been successfully sent and the app has checked the result. The settings page will identify the files still waiting, rather than show the folder as completely cleared. This may make the change appear slower, but we prefer a visible delay to making users uncertain about whether their latest work has been preserved.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: We considered offering one button that would remove all offline copies immediately. Several interview participants liked its simplicity, especially when they were preparing a shared laptop for another colleague. However, they also expected the app to protect unfinished work without asking them to inspect every file. An immediate removal button could not meet that expectation in our current design. We will therefore release folder selection first and leave a broader clearing function for later work. The help text will explain the difference between removing an offline copy and deleting project content, using one short example rather than a long technical description.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: For existing users, every current offline setting will remain on after the update. We will not silently remove files to demonstrate the new feature. A message on the project page will invite users to review folders they no longer need offline, and it will link directly to the settings page. New project members will be asked to choose folders during setup. They can accept the project's suggested selection or change it before the first download begins. Project owners may recommend folders that support common tasks, but each member will control the selection for their own device because working conditions differ between sites.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Testing will focus on realistic transitions rather than only on switching folders while everything is quiet. We will include a file being edited, a laptop losing its connection, and a shared folder receiving a new file from another member. Testers will check both the visible messages and the final copies in the shared project. They will also turn a folder back on after its local copy has been removed. The app should show download progress without claiming that every file is ready immediately. A pilot group from the survey team will use the feature for one week before we invite all users to update.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Support colleagues will receive a short guide with examples of the three main states: available offline, waiting for changes, and available when connected. They should begin a conversation by asking what the user wants to do, rather than telling every caller to switch all folders on. During the pilot, we will record confusing messages and cases where people mistake local removal for shared deletion. If that confusion remains common, we will revise the wording before the wider release. Success means that users can manage their device space and still explain where their work is, not merely that the settings page receives many clicks.

title: Recognition procedure: giving credit for work behind a team result
summary: Quy trình ghi nhận đóng góp giúp nhóm tránh chỉ khen người trình bày cuối cùng, sử dụng ví dụ cụ thể và tôn trọng lựa chọn được ghi nhận riêng tư.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: At last month's staff meeting, the customer portal team received praise for completing a difficult launch. The presentation named the engineer who demonstrated the finished product, but it did not mention colleagues who had checked instructions, answered trial users, or prepared the support schedule. Nobody intended to exclude them. However, several employees said the announcement made the result appear to depend on one visible contribution. This procedure introduces a clearer way to prepare recognition messages for shared work. It should help managers describe what people actually contributed without turning every announcement into a long list of names with no explanation of their roles.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Before writing a recognition message, the manager should ask the project team for examples of work that helped achieve the result. The request should include preparation, coordination, checking, and follow-up, as well as the final delivery. Team members may suggest their own work or another colleague's contribution. Each suggestion should describe an action and its effect. For example, 'Lan checked the setup guide with two new users and found a missing step' gives useful evidence. A phrase such as 'Lan was amazing' expresses appreciation but does not explain the contribution. The manager can ask for a clearer example without dismissing the original praise.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The manager should then compare the suggestions with project records and discuss unclear points with the people involved. This is not a competition to discover who worked the longest hours. Time spent can provide context, but a short action may have prevented a large problem. Equally, the absence of a person's name from a meeting note does not prove that they contributed nothing. Some useful work happens in quiet conversations or routine checks. The aim is a fair description supported by specific examples, rather than a score for every employee. If the evidence is incomplete, the message should avoid making broad claims about individual impact.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: People differ in how they like to receive recognition. Before naming someone in a public announcement, the manager should ask whether they are comfortable with that format. A colleague may prefer a private message or a note shared only with their immediate team. That preference should not be interpreted as a lack of interest in the project. Managers should also check how names are written and whether a person wants their role included. The communication team will provide a short preparation form so these details can be collected consistently. Completing the form should happen early enough to allow a genuine choice before the announcement is scheduled.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: We considered asking every employee to nominate one person each month. That would be easy to organise, but it might favour colleagues whose work is widely visible or whose teams are larger. It could also make people feel they must select someone even when they have no clear example. The new process will therefore begin with completed team results, rather than a fixed monthly voting round. Managers can still recognise a useful individual action when it occurs. They should explain what happened and why it mattered, instead of waiting for the person to receive enough nominations to appear on a popularity list.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: A public message should usually describe the shared result first, then give a few concrete examples of different contributions. Where many people were involved, the manager can link to a fuller team note approved by those being named. The short message should not imply that its examples cover every useful action. If a contribution is accidentally missed, the manager should correct the record promptly and speak with the affected colleague. A correction can be brief and factual. It is better to add accurate information than to defend an incomplete announcement because changing it feels awkward in front of the wider organisation.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: We will try the procedure with three teams over the next two months. After each announcement, employees can comment privately on whether the examples were clear and whether important work was overlooked. We will also ask managers how much preparation time the process required. A procedure that takes several days for a small achievement would discourage regular use, so the preparation form may need adjustment. Recognition messages will remain separate from formal performance decisions. Their purpose is to explain and appreciate useful work, while giving teams a better understanding of how different actions combine to produce a result that everyone can learn from.

title: Service estimate: restoring a home sewing machine for regular use
summary: Báo giá sửa máy may gia đình phân biệt công việc cần thiết và lựa chọn thêm, giải thích giới hạn thử nghiệm và hướng dẫn khách xác nhận trước khi sửa.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for bringing your sewing machine to our workshop on Tuesday. You explained that the thread sometimes breaks and that the machine has become difficult to control at low speed. You use it mainly for shortening curtains and repairing ordinary cotton clothes, rather than for heavy fabric or daily business work. We inspected the machine using the thread and sample cloth you supplied, then repeated the checks with our own materials. This estimate separates the work needed to address the problems we observed from optional improvements. Please read both sections before deciding, because the most expensive package is not automatically the best choice for your use.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: During the first test, the thread caught repeatedly at a rough point on the small guide above the needle. With a replacement guide fitted temporarily, the same thread passed through without catching during our sample run. We also found old thread pieces around the lower mechanism, which made its movement uneven in our inspection. We recommend replacing the guide and cleaning the lower area before adjusting the machine. These findings explain the problems reproduced in our workshop, but they do not prove that every future thread break will have the same cause. Thread quality, fabric, and setup can also vary between projects.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The standard service costs 680,000 dong, including the replacement guide, cleaning, adjustment, and a final test. We expect to complete it within four working days after you approve the estimate. The price covers the parts and labour listed here; it does not include an additional fault discovered after cleaning. If we find another problem that changes the proposed work, we will stop and contact you with a revised estimate. You may then approve the extra work or collect the machine after paying only for work already authorised and completed. We will not treat your approval of this estimate as permission for unlimited repairs.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The speed-control pedal also needs consideration. In our test, it produced a narrow range between no movement and a faster speed than you wanted. A replacement pedal gave us a wider usable range on this machine. Replacing it would add 420,000 dong to the standard service price. However, the existing pedal still operated during the test, so we have listed replacement as optional rather than included it automatically. You can try the machine after the standard service before deciding. If slow, careful sewing is important for most of your projects, that trial may help you judge whether the additional cost is worthwhile.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: You also asked whether we could add a brighter work light. We do not have a compatible replacement light in stock, and we have not included one in this estimate. Ordering a suitable part would require a separate check of availability and price. We considered delaying the whole service until we could give you a complete lighting quotation, but that would keep the machine here longer without helping us resolve the confirmed problems. Our recommendation is to complete the standard service first. The light can be discussed later, or you can decide that your existing desk lighting is sufficient for the way you sew.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: For the final test, we will use your sample cloth and make a second sample with two layers of ordinary cotton. We will check thread movement and control at several settings, then leave the samples attached to the service sheet. These tests match the uses you described, but they are not a promise that the machine can handle every heavy material. At collection, allow fifteen minutes to try the controls and ask questions about the work. Bring the thread you normally use if it differs from the thread already supplied. Your own short trial may reveal a practical concern that a workshop checklist does not capture.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: To approve the work, reply to our message with either 'standard service' or 'standard service with pedal'. If you are unsure about the pedal, choose the standard service and request a trial at collection. We will confirm the expected collection date once the work is booked. The estimate remains open for fourteen days; after that, we will check the part price again before accepting approval. If you decide against the service, please arrange collection so we can free space for other machines. There is no need to choose immediately at the counter, and we welcome questions about any item that is unclear.

title: Support investigation: a chart that compared unequal reporting periods
summary: Trao đổi hỗ trợ làm rõ biểu đồ so sánh một tháng chưa kết thúc với tháng đầy đủ, đề xuất cách hiển thị ngày và giữ lựa chọn phù hợp với từng mục đích.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: On 12 June, a customer contacted support because the activity chart in our booking system appeared to show a sudden fall in completed appointments. The chart displayed May and June as two columns, with June much lower. The customer had used the image in a weekly planning message, and colleagues were now asking whether demand had fallen. Before investigating possible missing records, support asked for the chart settings and the date on which the image had been captured. This exchange describes what we found and the proposed change. The customer's concern was reasonable because the image did not explain clearly how much time each column represented.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The chart was set to show completed appointments by calendar month. May represented the whole month, while June contained records only up to the morning of 12 June. The values matched the appointments stored for those periods in our checks. We did not find a missing group of records behind the lower column. The problem was the comparison: a completed month stood beside an unfinished month without an obvious difference in presentation. The customer had understood both columns as equivalent reporting periods. A small note below the chart mentioned the capture date, but it did not state that June was still in progress.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Support offered two ways to prepare a clearer planning message immediately. The customer could select the last two completed months, or compare the first twelve days of May with the first twelve days of June. These options answer different questions. Completed months help describe full monthly activity, while matching partial periods helps discuss the current month's progress. Support did not tell the customer which business conclusion to draw from either view. Instead, we asked what the planning message needed to explain. The customer chose matching partial periods because the team wanted to discuss recent activity before deciding how to arrange the remaining June sessions.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: When the customer created the matching-period chart, June remained lower than May, but the difference was much smaller than in the original image. This did not prove why activity had changed. The customer noted that several regular sessions had moved to later in June, which might help explain the timing. Our system held appointment dates, but it did not contain every reason behind scheduling decisions. Support therefore avoided describing the chart as proof of reduced demand. The revised planning message included the exact dates compared and asked team leads to add relevant context. This allowed the team to discuss the figures without overstating what they showed.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: For the product change, we considered hiding unfinished months from every monthly chart. That would make comparisons simpler, but it would also remove information that some customers use to monitor current activity. We propose keeping the unfinished period visible and marking it as incomplete in the column label. The chart title will state the date range, and the exported image will include that information too. This matters because an image can be separated from the settings page and shared with people who never opened the app. A clear explanation inside the image is more useful than instructions available only to its original creator.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: We will also add a comparison choice labelled 'same number of days'. When selected, it will show the dates used for each period before the chart is generated. The preview is important because months have different lengths and customers may have different expectations about the final day included. We will not automatically switch existing saved charts to this choice. A saved chart may support a regular report whose owner expects completed calendar periods. During testing, colleagues from support will review examples created near the beginning and end of a month, checking whether the dates remain understandable when the image is viewed on its own.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The customer has agreed to review the proposed labels using a practice account before release. We will ask her to explain what each sample chart compares without showing the settings that produced it. If she needs to guess, the labels require more work. Support will update its guide to distinguish missing data from an unclear comparison, while still checking both possibilities when a customer reports an unexpected result. We expect the change to reduce misleading screenshots, but we will review new support cases after release rather than assume the problem is solved. Accurate values are useful only when readers also understand the periods those values describe.
